newsitem.title: USA: Jury convicts teen in Brooklyn subway torching.
newsitem.headline: Jury convicts teen in Brooklyn subway torching.

text.p: A third teenager was convicted of murder Wednesday in the death of a subway token clerk who was set afire in his booth during a robbery attempt in Brooklyn one year ago.
The attack on 50-year-old Harry Kaufman gained national attention because it mirrored one depicted in the movie "Money Train" in which a pyromaniac torched two subway token booths.

In Wednesday's verdict, jurors found Thomas Malik, 19, guilty of lighting the gasoline inside the booth during the Nov. 26, 1995 incident. Two other Brooklyn teenagers were previously convicted of second degree murder.

The suspects denied that the movie starring Wesley Snipes and Woody Harrelson had anything to do with the attack. At the trial, prosecutors said the teens planned the robbery last Thanksgiving so they could have money to buy Christmas gifts.

Vincent Ellerbe, 18, who was tried with Malik but with a separate jury, was found guilty Tuesday. Both he and Malik face 25 years to life when sentenced by State Supreme Court Justice Francis Egitto Dec. 17.

Proscutors said Ellerbe squirted the gasoline into the money coin slot. Another teenager, James Irons, 19, was convicted last month for his role as the lookout. He was sentenced to 25 years to life on Nov. 18.
Kaufman was seen running and screaming from the scene, his clothes aflame. He was burned over 70 percent of his body and died two weeks later.
